title: Watermelon Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Watermelon Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Watermelon nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and potassium in pakwan, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Watermelon nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your pakwan (watermelon) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, potassium, magnesium, calcium, boron, phosphorus and zinc. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Potassium deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for watermelon

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But calcium, boron and zinc stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which watermelon nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a watermelon nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest watermelon nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in watermelon

Older leaves turn pale, yellow and drop, and the yellowing moves up the runners. Vines are stunted, and fruits are pale, small, thick skinned or misshapen, so yield falls. You see it most at this stage: vine growth and fruit set.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in pakwan
Sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, low organic matter and no side dressing before fruit set.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage leaves the veins green. Fusarium wilt makes whole runners wilt and the stem turns brown inside. To be sure, old leaves yellow first. Soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, before the fruits form. For a quick fix, KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, put part of the nitrogen in before planting and side dress the rest in one or two doses, as the University of Kentucky advises for cucurbits.
Potassium deficiency in watermelon

Older leaves yellow and scorch, then curl upward or cup, with sunken dark spots along the midrib. Browning spreads until leaves dry out. Shoots die back, stems weaken and fewer female flowers form. Fruits can have poor flesh texture, off flavour or spotted skin. You see it most at this stage: fruit filling.
Why potassium deficiency happens in pakwan
Sandy or acid soils, heavy rain or irrigation, and fertilizing with urea only.
How to tell it apart
Gummy stem blight and anthracnose also brown the leaves, but as spreading spots that start anywhere on the leaf. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, preferably in split doses. For immediate relief, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker. Keep soil pH above 6 with lime or dolomite.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash at planting and again as fruits enlarge.
Magnesium deficiency in watermelon

Mature leaves turn yellow in the middle with green edges and green veins. The yellow areas turn red and develop spotted dead patches, older leaves shrivel and drop early, and yield falls. You see it most at this stage: fruit enlargement.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in pakwan
Sandy acid soils, dry years, and heavy potash, lime or ammonium fertilizer.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage yellows the whole leaf. Manganese toxicity on very acid soil gives bronze spots on old leaves. To be sure, soil test for magnesium, potassium and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency

KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). The University of Kentucky advises keeping pH near 6.5, feeding Epsom salt through drip lines if needed. Notes leaf sprays rarely fix a serious shortage. Do not apply magnesium with potash.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil before planting.
Calcium deficiency in watermelon

Developing fruits rot at the blossom end, opposite the stem, starting as a sunken, leathery patch. Young leaves show yellow stripes along the midrib, crinkle and scorch at the edges, and new leaf tips hook. Growing points can die back, roots are stunted, and fruits may be small or tasteless. You see it most at this stage: early fruit growth.
Why calcium deficiency happens in pakwan

Uneven or too little watering, high humidity, poor root growth or anything else that slows water flow, which leaves the fruit short of calcium for a while. Heavy ammonium fertilizer, root injury and waterlogged soil make it worse.
How to tell it apart

Poor pollination gives shrivelled, misshapen young fruits without a leathery rot. Fruit rots from fungi are soft and mouldy. To be sure, look for the rot on young fruits after dry spells. Soil test for calcium and pH.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Give steady, proper irrigation, avoid root injury and waterlogging, and avoid heavy ammonium fertilizer, as the University of Kentucky advises. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soil before planting and keep watering even.
Boron deficiency in watermelon

Young leaves are malformed and buds die, making the plant bushy. Young fruits drop or abort, and fruits show mottled yellow streaks, corky scurf on the skin, cracks, small size and early fall. You see it most at this stage: flowering and fruit set.
Why boron deficiency happens in pakwan
Sandy soils, overlimed soils, low organic matter and drought.
How to tell it apart
Poor pollination also drops young fruits but leaves stay normal. Thrips scarring on fruit skin is silvery rather than corky streaks. To be sure, soil test for boron and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for boron deficiency
KAU suggests borax in the soil at about 10 kg per hectare (4 kg per acre) or a borax spray at 1 gram per liter of water. Do not mix borax with calcium or ammonium fertilizer.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add a small boron dose to the basal fertilizer on sandy fields.
Phosphorus deficiency in watermelon

Older leaves turn purple, especially along the veins. Shoots are short and thin, young leaves are small, stiff and dark green, leaves look dull and shrivel, and vigour and yield drop. You see it most at this stage: early vine growth.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in pakwan
Acid or iron rich soils, low organic matter, cold or waterlogged soil, and no phosphorus at planting.
How to tell it apart
Root knot nematodes also stunt vines. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply phosphorus in the hill based on the soil test. KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term, with best uptake near pH 6.2 to 7.0.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use complete fertilizer or 16 20 0 in the hill at planting.
Zinc deficiency in watermelon

Young leaves yellow between the veins and can turn white. Leaves are pale with green veins and smaller, the spaces between leaves are short, and leaves form distorted rosettes. You see it most at this stage: vine growth.
Why zinc deficiency happens in pakwan
High pH or overlimed soils, heavy phosphorus and waterlogged soils.
How to tell it apart
Mosaic viruses also give small, mottled leaves, often with aphids around. To be sure, soil test for zinc and pH, and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

KAU suggests zinc sulfate in the soil at about 20 kg per hectare (8 kg per acre). In severe cases a morning spray of zinc sulfate at 2 grams plus calcium carbonate at 2.5 grams per liter of water. Do not apply zinc and phosphate together.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep soil pH between 5 and 7.5.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any watermelon nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your pakwan needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Watermelon nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my pakwan leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: old leaves pale and yellow up the runner, with small, misshapen fruits. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at zinc deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in watermelon?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate based on the soil test, before the fruits form. For a quick fix, KAU gives a urea leaf spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in watermelon?
items.a: Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, preferably in split doses. For immediate relief, KAU gives a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes magnesium deficiency in watermelon?
items.a: KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). The University of Kentucky advises keeping pH near 6.5, feeding Epsom salt through drip lines if needed.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my pakwan lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the watermelon nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
